messages:
From: Jonathan Reyes <jonathan.reyes@curahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@curahealth.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test windowing for MSA/Order Form

Hi Mina / Laura,

Thanks for sharing the MSA and Order Form draft. As part of CuraHealth's procurement review we need to lock down the security exhibit and audit rights language before we proceed to signature. There are three items our security team is focused on:

- SOC 2 evidence cadence (what reports/artifacts we get and how often)
- Pen test notice window and permitted test types (and any staging vs production constraints)
- Scope and mechanics for audit access (read-only log access, timing, third-party assessor)

Can you confirm Redwood's preferred approach to (a) frequency of SOC2 reports and attachment delivery, (b) what constitutes "reasonable" notice for a pen test and whether we need to route through support or a security contact, and (c) whether you can provide temporary read-only S3 access or a snapshot export for evidence?

We can be flexible, but we need the language in the security exhibit to be reasonably prescriptive so our legal can close the loop. Attached is a short PDF with CuraHealth's baseline requirements.

Attachments: CuraHealth_security_requirements.pdf (summary)

Appreciate a quick sync this week if possible.

Best,
Jonathan Reyes
Director, Security & Compliance
CuraHealth
jonathan.reyes@curahealth.com

--

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test windowing for MSA/Order Form

Jonathan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. I can own coordination from product/security side and will loop legal for contract language. Quick answers up front:

- SOC 2: we provide SOC 2 Type II reports annually and can provide a redacted bridge letter / executive summary on a quarterly cadence where required.
- Pen test: standard is 30 days notice + a mutually agreed 3–5 day testing window, with production testing permitted only with an agreed scope and a dedicated rollback plan.
- Evidence access: we can provide read-only export of audit logs (S3 snapshot or pre-signed URLs) or a temporary role for a third-party assessor under an NDA / scoped access.

I'll have Laura share suggested redline language for the security exhibit (MSA) and a separate Order Form clause for pen-test scheduling. Can we set a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT?

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test windowing for MSA/Order Form

Jonathan / Mina / Karthik —

Attached is a proposed mark (cura_redlines_msa_v1.docx) that addresses the points Jonathan raised. High-level summary of what we added:

1) SOC 2 evidence: Redwood will deliver SOC 2 Type II reports annually and provide a non-technical executive summary quarterly upon request. We added a clause that any additional artifact requests must be limited to a reasonable scope and a documented request process (to avoid open-ended production-level data pulls).

2) Pen-testing: added a pen-test clause that requires a minimum 30 days advance notice, a mutually agreed scope, and a 3 business-day test window by default. Production testing will be permitted only with explicit written agreement and a shared rollback plan. We included a requirement that tests be run by a certified third-party assessor and that any destructive techniques are pre-approved.

3) Audit mechanics: proposed read-only access via time-limited pre-signed S3 URLs or a secure export bundle; we capped the audit access frequency to no more than twice per rolling 12 months unless by mutual written agreement (exceptions for regulatory audit). We also added a requirement for a signed NDA and a single point of contact at CuraHealth.

Please review the redlines and let me know any narrow edits you need. If CuraHealth requires more frequent access or raw production-level extracts, we will need to move that into a custom addendum with associated fees and SRE support commitments.

Attachment: cura_redlines_msa_v1.docx (MS Word redline)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jonathan Reyes <jonathan.reyes@curahealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks — will review and get back with any edits. One question: could you clarify what you mean by 'non-technical executive summary' and the exact artifacts included in that quarterly deliverable?

From: Jonathan Reyes <jonathan.reyes@curahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@curahealth.com, security@eversafe.com
Date: Thu, 5 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test windowing for MSA/Order Form

Laura / Mina —

Thanks for the redline — overall it looks good and aligns with our expectations. Quick clarifications:

- Executive summary: should include scope of the SOC 2 engagement, control environment changes since the last report, and any open remediation items that affect confidentiality/integrity (redacted where necessary). A one-page summary is fine but we need the ability to request follow-up details through a documented process.
- Audit frequency: the cap of twice per 12 months is acceptable for scheduled audits; CuraHealth will reserve the right to request a targeted access if there is a security incident.
- Access mechanics: can you confirm the export format (CSV + gzipped logs or pre-signed S3 URLs) and whether those exports will include request_id traces and timestamps (we need them for our downstream monitoring correlation).

I'm attaching CuraHealth_security_requirements.pdf for reference. If those items are okay, our legal team will prepare a short counter-redline that keeps the spirit of your draft but clarifies export formats and contact details.

Attachment: CuraHealth_security_requirements.pdf

Best,
Jonathan
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Reyes <jonathan.reyes@curahealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test windowing for MSA/Order Form

Jonathan —

Appreciate the clear note. From an operations/engineering standpoint we can support the following, which I captured as bullet points you can include in the exhibit or the Order Form attachment: 

- SOC2 artifacts: annual full SOC2 Type II PDF (redacted for third-party info), quarterly one-page executive summary (PDF).
- Export format & access: audit exports can be delivered as gzipped CSVs containing request_id, timestamp, endpoint, response_code, and top-level headers; alternatively, we can provide time-limited pre-signed S3 URLs to a snapshot bundle. We will not provide live direct DB queries.
- Pen test mechanics: 30 days notice + 3 business day testing window by default. Production testing permitted only with written approval and a rollback plan; destructive testing must be explicitly listed and approved.
- Access frequency: scheduled audits no more than twice per rolling 12 months. Targeted access for active incidents will be handled under an incident response process and will not count toward the scheduled audit cap.

Links and attachments: SOC2-Report-2026.pdf (annual report) is available on our secure drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CuraHealth/DH-4821/audit-pack
I also attached a short pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx that maps permitted techniques to environment (staging, pre-prod, prod) and risk acceptance.

If you confirm format (gzipped CSV vs pre-signed S3 bundle) and the single point-of-contact for scheduling, we'll add a short operational appendix to the Order Form describing delivery cadence and contact details.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-Report-2026.pdf, pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx
